svg.title: Tiny Agent Lab — Inference Provider Selection & Fallback
svg.desc: Subsystem architecture reference diagram (V4) illustrating the primary 1-to-9 execution flow: per-task health check, deterministic provider selection, provider invocation, fallback loop, explicit Task Complete terminal endpoint, parallel one-way operational telemetry streams, and Prototype Console observability in Tiny Agent Lab v0.4.0.

g.text: Tiny Agent Lab — Inference Provider Selection & Fallback
Subsystem Architecture • Released in v0.4.0 • The Autonomous Agent Inference Resilience Loop
• Probes priority chain: Provider A → B → C → ...
• Isolated: 1 failed probe never blocks others
• Priority breaks ties within same health class
• v0.4 examples: Cloudflare Workers AI, Google Gemini
Health checks, selection, events, & result persistence are excluded.
• Task output persisted to result store
Success Endpoint • Result Persisted • Agent Idle
• Selects next candidate in ranked chain
• Worker resets to idle; Research retains error
• Sliding-window event log (not a durable data warehouse)
• Timeline: failed → target provider, switch reason & 1-based attempt #
• Telemetry Card: successful attempt via task-scoped query
displays provider, model, execution latency ms & attempt #
• Task Result: formatted output from result store API (not stream)
Quarantined credentials: zero secrets or raw tracebacks exposed
Console presentation observes completion; it does not cause completion
Inclusion in configuration does not prove live availability.
Ranking as Candidate #1 does not guarantee inference succeeds.
Missing health snapshots are excluded; never treated as healthy.
Each provider attempt produces exactly one telemetry record.
No Fabricated State: Never fabricate health status, token counts, or duplicate attempt records.
Steps 1 → 2 → 3 → 4: Task initiation, health checks, candidate selection
Steps 5 → 6 → TASK COMPLETE: Response returned, persisted, agent idle
Steps 7 → 8 → 4: Eligible transient error, advance candidate & retry
Step 9: Terminal error, chain exhausted, or 0 eligible candidates (stop / fail)
• Arbitrary Provider Priority: Provider A → Provider B → Provider C → ... (v0.4 examples: Cloudflare, Gemini)
